title: Viewport and container-relative thinking
learningObjectives: Explain viewport and container-relative thinking and choose suitable CSS values for a responsive layout.

understand.concept: Viewport-relative units respond to the browser viewport. Container queries and container query units allow components to respond to the size of a declared ancestor container. Container-relative units include cqw and cqh, while @container enables conditional styling based on container size.
understand.whyItMatters: A component may appear in a narrow sidebar or a wide main region on the same viewport. Container-aware design makes reusable components adapt to their available space rather than assuming the whole screen is the reference.
understand.analogy: A viewport is the whole room; a container is the particular desk where a component must fit. A reusable component should often respond to its desk.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual sizing follows CSS value resolution and layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The heading uses a container-relative unit and the card layout changes when its container reaches the query threshold.

practise.guidedTask: Place the same card in narrow and wide containers. Use @container to switch from stacked to two-column layout.
practise.independentTask: Create a small responsive component using the concept. Test narrow and wide viewports, long text, and browser zoom.

questions.prompt: What does a container query use as its sizing reference?
options: A universal unit that always means pixels
questions.explanation: Container queries evaluate the size or state of a query container, not merely the viewport.

questions.prompt: How should you choose a CSS unit?
options: Match the unit to the desired sizing relationship
Always use px for every property
questions.answer: Match the unit to the desired sizing relationship
questions.explanation: The unit's reference and responsive behaviour should match the design requirement.
